class HVACOptimizer(nn.Module):
    """
    Optimizes HVAC system for comfort and energy efficiency.
    Considers thermal dynamics, occupancy, and weather.
    """
    def __init__(self, indoor_features: int, outdoor_features: int, 
                 occupancy_features: int):
        super(HVACOptimizer, self).__init__()
        
        # Indoor condition encoder (temperature, humidity, CO2)
        self.indoor_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(indoor_features, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64)
        )
        
        # Outdoor weather encoder
        self.outdoor_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(outdoor_features, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64)
        )
        
        # Occupancy pattern encoder
        self.occupancy_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(occupancy_features, 32),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Thermal dynamics model (predicts temperature change)
        self.dynamics_model = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(64 + 64 + 32, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # HVAC control outputs
        self.temperature_setpoint = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()  # Normalized setpoint
        )
        
        self.fan_speed = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        self.ventilation_rate = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
    def forward(self, indoor: torch.Tensor, outdoor: torch.Tensor, 
                occupancy: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
        """
        Args:
            indoor: Indoor conditions (batch_size, indoor_features)
            outdoor: Outdoor weather (batch_size, outdoor_features)
            occupancy: Occupancy data (batch_size, occupancy_features)
        Returns:
            Dictionary of HVAC control parameters
        """
        indoor_feat = self.indoor_encoder(indoor)
        outdoor_feat = self.outdoor_encoder(outdoor)
        occupancy_feat = self.occupancy_encoder(occupancy)
        
        combined = torch.cat([indoor_feat, outdoor_feat, occupancy_feat], dim=1)
        dynamics = self.dynamics_model(combined)
        
        controls = {
            'temperature_setpoint': self.temperature_setpoint(dynamics),
            'fan_speed': self.fan_speed(dynamics),
            'ventilation_rate': self.ventilation_rate(dynamics)
        }
        
        return controls


# ============================================================================
# 3311. Fault Detection in Energy Systems Pattern
# ============================================================================

class EnergySystemFaultDetector(nn.Module):
    """
    Detects anomalies and faults in energy systems using autoencoder approach.
    Identifies deviations from normal operating patterns.
    """
    def __init__(self, input_features: int, latent_dim: int = 32):
        super(EnergySystemFaultDetector, self).__init__()
        
        # Encoder
        self.encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_features, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(128),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64),
            nn.Linear(64, latent_dim),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Decoder
        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64),
            nn.Linear(64, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(128),
            nn.Linear(128, input_features)
        )
        
        # Fault classifier (uses latent representation)
        self.fault_classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 10),  # 10 fault types
            nn.Softmax(dim=1)
        )
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Args:
            x: System measurements (batch_size, input_features)
        Returns:
            Tuple of (reconstructed, fault_probabilities, latent_representation)
        """
        latent = self.encoder(x)
        reconstructed = self.decoder(latent)
        fault_probs = self.fault_classifier(latent)
        
        return reconstructed, fault_probs, latent
    
    def detect_anomaly(self, x: torch.Tensor, threshold: float = 0.1) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Detect anomalies based on reconstruction error.
        """
        reconstructed, _, _ = self.forward(x)
        reconstruction_error = torch.mean((x - reconstructed) ** 2, dim=1)
        anomalies = reconstruction_error > threshold
        return anomalies


# ============================================================================
# 3312. Predictive Maintenance for Energy Pattern
# ============================================================================

class PredictiveMaintenanceSystem(nn.Module):
    """
    Predicts equipment failure and maintenance needs in energy systems.
    Uses temporal sensor data to estimate remaining useful life (RUL).
    """
    def __init__(self, sensor_features: int, seq_len: int, num_equipment_types: int = 5):
        super(PredictiveMaintenanceSystem, self).__init__()
        
        # Temporal feature extraction
        self.feature_extractor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv1d(sensor_features, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64),
            nn.Conv1d(64, 128, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(128),
            nn.MaxPool1d(2)
        )
        
        # LSTM for degradation pattern learning
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(128, 256, num_layers=2, batch_first=True, dropout=0.2)
        
        # Attention mechanism
        self.attention = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.Tanh(),
            nn.Linear(128, 1)
        )
        
        # RUL (Remaining Useful Life) predictor
        self.rul_predictor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 1),
            nn.ReLU()  # RUL is positive
        )
        
        # Failure probability estimator
        self.failure_prob = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(256, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        # Equipment type classifier
        self.equipment_classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, num_equipment_types),
            nn.Softmax(dim=1)
        )
        
    def forward(self, sensor_data: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
        """
        Args:
            sensor_data: Time series sensor data (batch_size, sensor_features, seq_len)
        Returns:
            Dictionary with RUL, failure probability, and equipment type
        """
        # Feature extraction
        features = self.feature_extractor(sensor_data)
        features = features.permute(0, 2, 1)  # (batch, seq, features)
        
        # LSTM processing
        lstm_out, (hidden, _) = self.lstm(features)
        
        # Attention weights
        attention_weights = torch.softmax(self.attention(lstm_out), dim=1)
        context = torch.sum(attention_weights * lstm_out, dim=1)
        
        # Predictions
        predictions = {
            'rul': self.rul_predictor(context),
            'failure_probability': self.failure_prob(context),
            'equipment_type': self.equipment_classifier(context)
        }
        
        return predictions

# 3313. Carbon Emission Prediction Pattern
# ============================================================================

class CarbonEmissionPredictor(nn.Module):
    """
    Predicts carbon emissions based on energy consumption and source mix.
    Accounts for different energy sources and their emission factors.
    """
    def __init__(self, energy_features: int, source_types: int, 
                 external_features: int):
        super(CarbonEmissionPredictor, self).__init__()
        
        # Energy consumption encoder
        self.energy_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(energy_features, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64)
        )
        
        # Energy source mix encoder
        self.source_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(source_types, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(32)
        )
        
        # External factors (weather, economic activity, etc.)
        self.external_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(external_features, 32),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Emission calculation network
        self.emission_calculator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(64 + 32 + 32, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
            nn.ReLU()  # Emissions are positive
        )
        
        # Uncertainty estimator
        self.uncertainty = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(64 + 32 + 32, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
```python
            nn.Linear(64, 1),
            nn.Softplus()  # Positive uncertainty
        )
        
    def forward(self, energy_data: torch.Tensor, source_mix: torch.Tensor,
                external_factors: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Args:
            energy_data: Energy consumption data (batch_size, energy_features)
            source_mix: Energy source distribution (batch_size, source_types)
            external_factors: External variables (batch_size, external_features)
        Returns:
            Tuple of (predicted_emissions, uncertainty)
        """
        energy_feat = self.energy_encoder(energy_data)
        source_feat = self.source_encoder(source_mix)
        external_feat = self.external_encoder(external_factors)
        
        combined = torch.cat([energy_feat, source_feat, external_feat], dim=1)
        
        emissions = self.emission_calculator(combined)
        uncertainty = self.uncertainty(combined)
        
        return emissions, uncertainty


# ============================================================================
# 3314. Environmental Monitoring Pattern
# ============================================================================

class EnvironmentalMonitor(nn.Module):
    """
    Multi-sensor environmental monitoring system.
    Processes diverse sensor types for comprehensive environmental assessment.
    """
    def __init__(self, num_sensor_types: int, sensors_per_type: int,
                 spatial_dim: int = 2):
        super(EnvironmentalMonitor, self).__init__()
        
        self.num_sensor_types = num_sensor_types
        
        # Spatial encoder (GPS coordinates or grid positions)
        self.spatial_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(spatial_dim, 16),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(16, 32),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Per-sensor-type encoders
        self.sensor_encoders = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(sensors_per_type, 64),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.BatchNorm1d(64),
                nn.Linear(64, 32),
                nn.ReLU()
            ) for _ in range(num_sensor_types)
        ])
        
        # Cross-sensor attention
        self.cross_attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(
            embed_dim=32, num_heads=4, batch_first=True
        )
        
        # Environmental state aggregator
        self.state_aggregator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(32 * num_sensor_types + 32, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Multiple output heads
        self.air_quality_head = nn.Linear(128, 1)
        self.pollution_level_head = nn.Linear(128, 1)
        self.anomaly_score_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
    def forward(self, sensor_data: List[torch.Tensor], 
                locations: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
        """
        Args:
            sensor_data: List of sensor readings per type (batch_size, sensors_per_type)
            locations: Spatial coordinates (batch_size, spatial_dim)
        Returns:
            Dictionary of environmental metrics
        """
        # Encode spatial information
        spatial_feat = self.spatial_encoder(locations)
        
        # Encode each sensor type
        sensor_features = []
        for data, encoder in zip(sensor_data, self.sensor_encoders):
            sensor_features.append(encoder(data))
        
        # Stack for attention
        sensor_stack = torch.stack(sensor_features, dim=1)  # (batch, num_types, 32)
        
        # Apply cross-sensor attention
        attended_features, _ = self.cross_attention(
            sensor_stack, sensor_stack, sensor_stack
        )
        attended_features = attended_features.reshape(attended_features.size(0), -1)
        
        # Combine with spatial features
        combined = torch.cat([attended_features, spatial_feat], dim=1)
        state = self.state_aggregator(combined)
        
        # Generate outputs
        outputs = {
            'air_quality_index': self.air_quality_head(state),
            'pollution_level': self.pollution_level_head(state),
            'anomaly_score': self.anomaly_score_head(state)
        }
        
        return outputs


# ============================================================================
# 3315. Air Quality Prediction Pattern
# ============================================================================

class AirQualityPredictor(nn.Module):
    """
    Predicts air quality index (AQI) and pollutant concentrations.
    Incorporates meteorological data and emission sources.
    """
    def __init__(self, pollutant_features: int, weather_features: int,
                 temporal_features: int, forecast_hours: int = 24):
        super(AirQualityPredictor, self).__init__()
        
        self.forecast_hours = forecast_hours
        
        # Current pollutant encoder
        self.pollutant_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(pollutant_features, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64),
            nn.Dropout(0.2)
        )
        
        # Weather condition encoder
        self.weather_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(weather_features, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64)
        )
        
        # Temporal pattern encoder (hour, day, season)
        self.temporal_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(temporal_features, 32),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # LSTM for temporal dynamics
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(64 + 64 + 32, 128, num_layers=2, 
                           batch_first=True, dropout=0.2)
        
        # Decoder for multi-hour forecast
        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(128, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, forecast_hours * 6)  # 6 major pollutants
        )
        
        # AQI calculator
        self.aqi_calculator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(forecast_hours * 6, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, forecast_hours),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
    def forward(self, pollutants: torch.Tensor, weather: torch.Tensor,
                temporal: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Args:
            pollutants: Current pollutant levels (batch_size, pollutant_features)
            weather: Weather conditions (batch_size, weather_features)
            temporal: Temporal features (batch_size, temporal_features)
        Returns:
            Tuple of (pollutant_forecast, aqi_forecast)
        """
        pollutant_feat = self.pollutant_encoder(pollutants)
        weather_feat = self.weather_encoder(weather)
        temporal_feat = self.temporal_encoder(temporal)
        
        # Combine features
        combined = torch.cat([pollutant_feat, weather_feat, temporal_feat], dim=1)
        combined = combined.unsqueeze(1)  # Add sequence dimension
        
        # LSTM processing
        lstm_out, _ = self.lstm(combined)
        
        # Forecast pollutants
        pollutant_forecast = self.decoder(lstm_out[:, -1, :])
        pollutant_forecast = pollutant_forecast.view(-1, self.forecast_hours, 6)
        
        # Calculate AQI
        aqi_forecast = self.aqi_calculator(pollutant_forecast.view(-1, self.forecast_hours * 6))
        
        return pollutant_forecast, aqi_forecast


# ============================================================================
# 3316. Water Quality Monitoring Pattern
# ============================================================================

class WaterQualityMonitor(nn.Module):
    """
    Monitors and predicts water quality parameters.
    Detects contamination and quality degradation.
    """
    def __init__(self, physical_params: int, chemical_params: int,
                 biological_params: int):
        super(WaterQualityMonitor, self).__init__()
        
        # Physical parameter encoder (temperature, turbidity, etc.)
        self.physical_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(physical_params, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(32)
        )
        
        # Chemical parameter encoder (pH, dissolved oxygen, etc.)
        self.chemical_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(chemical_params, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64),
            nn.Dropout(0.2)
        )
        
        # Biological parameter encoder (bacteria, algae, etc.)
        self.biological_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(biological_params, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(32)
        )
        
        # Integration network
        self.integrator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(32 + 64 + 32, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Water Quality Index (WQI) predictor
        self.wqi_predictor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()  # Normalized WQI
        )
        
        # Contamination detector
        self.contamination_detector = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        # Quality category classifier (excellent, good, fair, poor)
        self.category_classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 4),
            nn.Softmax(dim=1)
        )
        
    def forward(self, physical: torch.Tensor, chemical: torch.Tensor,
                biological: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
        """
        Args:
            physical: Physical parameters (batch_size, physical_params)
            chemical: Chemical parameters (batch_size, chemical_params)
            biological: Biological parameters (batch_size, biological_params)
        Returns:
            Dictionary of water quality metrics
        """
        phys_feat = self.physical_encoder(physical)
        chem_feat = self.chemical_encoder(chemical)
        bio_feat = self.biological_encoder(biological)
        
        combined = torch.cat([phys_feat, chem_feat, bio_feat], dim=1)
        integrated = self.integrator(combined)
        
        results = {
            'wqi': self.wqi_predictor(integrated),
            'contamination_probability': self.contamination_detector(integrated),
            'quality_category': self.category_classifier(integrated)
        }
        
        return results


# ============================================================================
# 3317. Waste Management Optimization Pattern
# ============================================================================

class WasteManagementOptimizer(nn.Module):
    """
    Optimizes waste collection routes and schedules.
    Predicts fill levels and optimizes resource allocation.
    """
    def __init__(self, num_bins: int, bin_features: int, 
                 route_features: int):
        super(WasteManagementOptimizer, self).__init__()
        
        self.num_bins = num_bins
        
        # Per-bin encoder (location, fill level, waste type)
        self.bin_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(bin_features, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64),
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Graph attention for spatial relationships
        self.spatial_attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(
            embed_dim=32, num_heads=4, batch_first=True
        )
        
        # Route optimizer
        self.route_optimizer = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(32 * num_bins + route_features, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, num_bins),
            nn.Softmax(dim=1)  # Priority scores for bins
        )
        
        # Fill level predictor (for each bin)
        self.fill_predictor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(32, 16),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(16, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        # Collection time estimator
        self.time_estimator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(num_bins, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 1),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
    def forward(self, bin_data: torch.Tensor, 
                route_constraints: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
        """
        Args:
            bin_data: Data for all bins (batch_size, num_bins, bin_features)
            route_constraints: Route constraints (batch_size, route_features)
        Returns:
            Dictionary with collection priorities and predictions
        """
        batch_size = bin_data.size(0)
        
        # Encode each bin
        bin_features = self.bin_encoder(bin_data.view(-1, bin_data.size(-1)))
        bin_features = bin_features.view(batch_size, self.num_bins, -1)
        
        # Apply spatial attention
        attended_bins, _ = self.spatial_attention(
            bin_features, bin_features, bin_features
        )
        
        # Flatten for route optimization
        flattened = attended_bins.view(batch_size, -1)
        combined = torch.cat([flattened, route_constraints], dim=1)
        
        # Optimize collection route
        priorities = self.route_optimizer(combined)
        
        # Predict fill levels
        fill_predictions = self.fill_predictor(attended_bins.view(-1, 32))
        fill_predictions = fill_predictions.view(batch_size, self.num_bins)
        
        # Estimate collection time
        collection_time = self.time_estimator(priorities)
        
        return {
            'collection_priorities': priorities,
            'predicted_fill_levels': fill_predictions,
            'estimated_time': collection_time
        }

class RecyclingClassifier(nn.Module):
    """
    Classifies waste items for recycling using multi-modal inputs.
    Combines visual, weight, and material composition data.
    """
    def __init__(self, image_channels: int = 3, sensor_features: int = 10,
                 num_categories: int = 7):
        super(RecyclingClassifier, self).__init__()
        
        # CNN for visual classification
        self.visual_encoder = nn.Sequential
```python
(
            # Image input processing
            nn.Conv2d(image_channels, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(32),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((4, 4))
        )
        
        # Sensor data encoder (weight, metal detector, etc.)
        self.sensor_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(sensor_features, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(64),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Multi-modal fusion
        self.fusion = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(128 * 4 * 4 + 32, 512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.4),
            nn.Linear(512, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Classification head
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, num_categories)
        )
        
        # Recyclability score
        self.recyclability = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(128, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        # Contamination detector
        self.contamination = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(128, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
    def forward(self, image: torch.Tensor, 
                sensors: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
        """
        Args:
            image: Visual input (batch_size, channels, height, width)
            sensors: Sensor readings (batch_size, sensor_features)
        Returns:
            Dictionary with classification and quality metrics
        """
        # Process visual information
        visual_features = self.visual_encoder(image)
        visual_features = visual_features.view(visual_features.size(0), -1)
        
        # Process sensor data
        sensor_features = self.sensor_encoder(sensors)
        
        # Fuse modalities
        combined = torch.cat([visual_features, sensor_features], dim=1)
        fused = self.fusion(combined)
        
        # Generate outputs
        results = {
            'category_logits': self.classifier(fused),
            'recyclability_score': self.recyclability(fused),
            'contamination_level': self.contamination(fused)
        }
        
        return results

# 3319. Climate Change Modeling Pattern
# ============================================================================

class ClimateChangeModel(nn.Module):
    """
    Models climate change trends and predictions.
    Incorporates atmospheric, oceanic, and terrestrial data.
    """
    def __init__(self, atmospheric_features: int, oceanic_features: int,
                 terrestrial_features: int, forecast_years: int = 10):
        super(ClimateChangeModel, self).__init__()
        
        self.forecast_years = forecast_years
        
        # Atmospheric encoder (temperature, CO2, etc.)
        self.atmospheric_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(atmospheric_features, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(128),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Oceanic encoder (sea level, temperature, currents)
        self.oceanic_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(oceanic_features, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(128),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Terrestrial encoder (ice coverage, vegetation, etc.)
        self.terrestrial_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(terrestrial_features, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(128),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Temporal dynamics model
        self.dynamics_lstm = nn.LSTM(
            64 + 64 + 64, 256, num_layers=3, 
            batch_first=True, dropout=0.3
        )
        
        # Multi-task prediction heads
        self.temperature_predictor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, forecast_years)
        )
        
        self.sea_level_predictor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, forecast_years),
            nn.ReLU()  # Sea level rise is positive
        )
        
        self.co2_predictor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, forecast_years),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        self.ice_coverage_predictor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, forecast_years),
            nn.Sigmoid()  # Normalized coverage
        )
        
        # Uncertainty estimator
        self.uncertainty = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(256, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, forecast_years),
            nn.Softplus()
        )
        
    def forward(self, atmospheric: torch.Tensor, oceanic: torch.Tensor,
                terrestrial: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
        """
        Args:
            atmospheric: Atmospheric data (batch_size, atmospheric_features)
            oceanic: Oceanic data (batch_size, oceanic_features)
            terrestrial: Terrestrial data (batch_size, terrestrial_features)
        Returns:
            Dictionary of climate predictions
        """
        atmos_feat = self.atmospheric_encoder(atmospheric)
        ocean_feat = self.oceanic_encoder(oceanic)
        terr_feat = self.terrestrial_encoder(terrestrial)
        
        # Combine all features
        combined = torch.cat([atmos_feat, ocean_feat, terr_feat], dim=1)
        combined = combined.unsqueeze(1)  # Add sequence dimension
        
        # Model temporal dynamics
        lstm_out, (hidden, _) = self.dynamics_lstm(combined)
        features = hidden[-1]
        
        # Generate predictions
        predictions = {
            'temperature_change': self.temperature_predictor(features),
            'sea_level_rise': self.sea_level_predictor(features),
            'co2_concentration': self.co2_predictor(features),
            'ice_coverage': self.ice_coverage_predictor(features),
            'uncertainty': self.uncertainty(features)
        }
        
        return predictions

# 3320. Extreme Weather Prediction Pattern
# ============================================================================

class ExtremeWeatherPredictor(nn.Module):
    """
    Predicts extreme weather events (hurricanes, floods, heatwaves, etc.).
    Uses spatio-temporal convolution and attention mechanisms.
    """
    def __init__(self, spatial_size: Tuple[int, int], num_channels: int,
                 num_event_types: int = 5, forecast_steps: int = 24):
        super(ExtremeWeatherPredictor, self).__init__()
        
        self.forecast_steps = forecast_steps
        self.num_event_types = num_event_types
        
        # Spatial feature extractor (for gridded weather data)
        self.spatial_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(num_channels, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            nn.Conv2d(128, 256, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(256),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2)
        )
        
        # Calculate spatial dimensions after pooling
        h_out = spatial_size[0] // 4
        w_out = spatial_size[1] // 4
        
        # Temporal encoder
        self.temporal_encoder = nn.LSTM(
            256 * h_out * w_out, 512, num_layers=2,
            batch_first=True, dropout=0.3
        )
        
        # Self-attention for identifying critical patterns
        self.attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(
            embed_dim=512, num_heads=8, batch_first=True
        )
        
        # Event probability predictor (per event type)
        self.event_predictor = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(512, 256),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.3),
                nn.Linear(256, forecast_steps),
                nn.Sigmoid()
            ) for _ in range(num_event_types)
        ])
        
        # Severity estimator
        self.severity_estimator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(512, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, num_event_types * forecast_steps),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        # Location predictor (spatial heatmap)
        self.location_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(512, 256 * h_out * w_out),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        self.location_upsampler = nn.Sequential(
            nn.ConvTranspose2d(256, 128, kernel_size=4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
            nn.ConvTranspose2d(128, 64, kernel_size=4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.Conv2d(64, num_event_types, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        self.h_out = h_out
        self.w_out = w_out
        
    def forward(self, weather_grid: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
        """
        Args:
            weather_grid: Gridded weather data 
                         (batch_size, seq_len, channels, height, width)
        Returns:
            Dictionary with event predictions, severity, and locations
        """
        batch_size, seq_len = weather_grid.size(0), weather_grid.size(1)
        
        # Process spatial features for each time step
        spatial_features = []
        for t in range(seq_len):
            feat = self.spatial_encoder(weather_grid[:, t])
            feat = feat.view(batch_size, -1)
            spatial_features.append(feat)
        
        # Stack temporal sequence
        temporal_input = torch.stack(spatial_features, dim=1)
        
        # LSTM for temporal patterns
        lstm_out, (hidden, _) = self.temporal_encoder(temporal_input)
        
        # Apply self-attention
        attended, _ = self.attention(lstm_out, lstm_out, lstm_out)
        final_features = attended[:, -1, :]
        
        # Predict event probabilities
        event_probs = [predictor(final_features) for predictor in self.event_predictor]
        event_probs = torch.stack(event_probs, dim=1)  # (batch, num_events, forecast_steps)
        
        # Predict severity
        severity = self.severity_estimator(final_features)
        severity = severity.view(batch_size, self.num_event_types, self.forecast_steps)
        
        # Predict spatial locations
        location_features = self.location_decoder(final_features)
        location_features = location_features.view(batch_size, 256, self.h_out, self.w_out)
        location_heatmap = self.location_upsampler(location_features)
        
        predictions = {
            'event_probabilities': event_probs,
            'severity': severity,
            'location_heatmap': location_heatmap
        }
        
        return predictions

class EnergyTimeSeriesDataset(Dataset):
    """
    Generic dataset for time series energy data.
    """
    def __init__(self, data: np.ndarray, targets: np.ndarray, 
                 seq_len: int = 24):
        """
        Args:
            data: Input features (num_samples, num_features)
            targets: Target values (num_samples, num_targets)
            seq_len: Sequence length for temporal data
        """
        self.data = torch.FloatTensor(data)
        self.targets = torch.FloatTensor(targets)
        self.seq_len = seq_len
        
    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.data) - self.seq_len
    
    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        x = self.data[idx:idx + self.seq_len]
        y = self.targets[idx + self.seq_len]
        return x, y


class MultiModalRecyclingDataset(Dataset):
    """
    Dataset for recycling classification with images and sensor data.
    """
    def __init__(self, images: np.ndarray, sensors: np.ndarray, 
                 labels: np.ndarray):
        """
        Args:
            images: Image data (num_samples, channels, height, width)
            sensors: Sensor readings (num_samples, num_sensors)
            labels: Classification labels (num_samples,)
        """
        self.images = torch.FloatTensor(images)
        self.sensors = torch.FloatTensor(sensors)
        self.labels = torch.LongTensor(labels)
        
    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.labels)
    
    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        return self.images[idx], self.sensors[idx], self.labels[idx]


class SpatialTemporalDataset(Dataset):
    """
    Dataset for spatio-temporal data (weather, climate, etc.).
    """
    def __init__(self, spatial_data: np.ndarray, temporal_features: np.n
```python

                 targets: np.ndarray):
        """
        Args:
            spatial_data: Gridded spatial data (num_samples, seq_len, channels, H, W)
            temporal_features: Temporal features (num_samples, temporal_dim)
            targets: Target values (num_samples, target_dim)
        """
        self.spatial_data = torch.FloatTensor(spatial_data)
        self.temporal_features = torch.FloatTensor(temporal_features)
        self.targets = torch.FloatTensor(targets)
        
    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.targets)
    
    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        return self.spatial_data[idx], self.temporal_features[idx], self.targets[idx]


# ============================================================================
# Training Utilities
# ============================================================================

class EnergyLoss(nn.Module):
    """
    Custom loss function for energy prediction tasks.
    Combines MSE with penalty for peak hour errors.
    """
    def __init__(self, peak_weight: float = 2.0):
        super(EnergyLoss, self).__init__()
        self.peak_weight = peak_weight
        self.mse = nn.MSELoss(reduction='none')
        
    def forward(self, predictions: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor,
                is_peak_hour: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Args:
            predictions: Model predictions
            targets: Ground truth values
            is_peak_hour: Binary mask for peak hours (optional)
        """
        loss = self.mse(predictions, targets)
        
        if is_peak_hour is not None:
            # Apply higher weight to peak hour errors
            weights = torch.where(is_peak_hour, 
                                 torch.tensor(self.peak_weight),
                                 torch.tensor(1.0))
            loss = loss * weights
            
        return loss.mean()


class UncertaintyLoss(nn.Module):
    """
    Loss function that accounts for prediction uncertainty.
    Uses negative log-likelihood with learned variance.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        super(UncertaintyLoss, self).__init__()
        
    def forward(self, predictions: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor,
                uncertainty: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Args:
            predictions: Model predictions
            targets: Ground truth values
            uncertainty: Predicted uncertainty (variance)
        """
        # Negative log-likelihood
        loss = 0.5 * torch.log(uncertainty) + \
               0.5 * ((predictions - targets) ** 2) / uncertainty
        return loss.mean()


def train_energy_model(model: nn.Module, train_loader: DataLoader,
                       val_loader: DataLoader, num_epochs: int = 100,
                       learning_rate: float = 0.001, device: str = 'cuda'):
    """
    Generic training function for energy prediction models.
    
    Args:
        model: PyTorch model to train
        train_loader: Training data loader
        val_loader: Validation data loader
        num_epochs: Number of training epochs
        learning_rate: Learning rate
        device: Device to train on ('cuda' or 'cpu')
    """
    model = model.to(device)
    optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
    scheduler = optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(
        optimizer, mode='min', factor=0.5, patience=5, verbose=True
    )
    criterion = nn.MSELoss()
    
    best_val_loss = float('inf')
    
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        # Training phase
        model.train()
        train_loss = 0.0
        
        for batch_idx, (data, target) in enumerate(train_loader):
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = model(data)
            loss = criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            
            # Gradient clipping for stability
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)
            
            optimizer.step()
            train_loss += loss.item()
        
        train_loss /= len(train_loader)
        
        # Validation phase
        model.eval()
        val_loss = 0.0
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for data, target in val_loader:
                data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
                output = model(data)
                loss = criterion(output, target)
                val_loss += loss.item()
        
        val_loss /= len(val_loader)
        
        # Learning rate scheduling
        scheduler.step(val_loss)
        
        # Save best model
        if val_loss < best_val_loss:
            best_val_loss = val_loss
            torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'best_energy_model.pth')
        
        if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
            print(f'Epoch [{epoch+1}/{num_epochs}], '
                  f'Train Loss: {train_loss:.4f}, '
                  f'Val Loss: {val_loss:.4f}')
    
    print(f'Training completed. Best validation loss: {best_val_loss:.4f}')

def train_solar_power_example():
    """
    Example of training a solar power prediction model.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("Training Example: Solar Power Prediction")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Generate synthetic data
    num_samples = 10000
    weather_features = np.random.randn(num_samples, 6)
    time_features = np.random.randn(num_samples, 3)
    
    # Simulate solar power output (simplified)
    solar_power = np.random.rand(num_samples, 1)
    
    # Create datasets
    from torch.utils.data import TensorDataset
    
    train_size = int(0.8 * num_samples)
    
    train_dataset = TensorDataset(
        torch.FloatTensor(weather_features[:train_size]),
        torch.FloatTensor(time_features[:train_size]),
        torch.FloatTensor(solar_power[:train_size])
    )
    
    val_dataset = TensorDataset(
        torch.FloatTensor(weather_features[train_size:]),
        torch.FloatTensor(time_features[train_size:]),
        torch.FloatTensor(solar_power[train_size:])
    )
    
    train_loader = DataLoader(train_dataset, batch_size=64, shuffle=True)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_dataset, batch_size=64)
    
    # Initialize model
    model = SolarPowerPredictor(input_features=6, hidden_size=128)
    
    # Training setup
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    model = model.to(device)
    optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn.MSELoss()
    
    # Training loop (simplified)
    num_epochs = 5
    print(f"\nTraining on {device}...")
    
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        model.train()
        train_loss = 0.0
        
        for weather, time, target in train_loader:
            weather, time, target = weather.to(device), time.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = model(weather, time)
            loss = criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            train_loss += loss.item()
        
        train_loss /= len(train_loader)
        
        # Validation
        model.eval()
        val_loss = 0.0
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for weather, time, target in val_loader:
                weather, time, target = weather.to(device), time.to(device), target.to(device)
                output = model(weather, time)
                loss = criterion(output, target)
                val_loss += loss.item()
        
        val_loss /= len(val_loader)
        
        print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs} - Train Loss: {train_loss:.6f}, Val Loss: {val_loss:.6f}")
    
    print("Training completed!")
    
    # Save model
    torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'solar_power_model.pth')
    print("Model saved to 'solar_power_model.pth'")


def evaluate_model_performance():
    """
    Example of evaluating model performance with various metrics.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("Model Evaluation Example")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Generate test data
    num_test = 1000
    predictions = torch.randn(num_test, 1)
    targets = torch.randn(num_test, 1)
    
    # Calculate metrics
    mse = torch.mean((predictions - targets) ** 2)
    mae = torch.mean(torch.abs(predictions - targets))
    rmse = torch.sqrt(mse)
    
    # R-squared
    ss_res = torch.sum((targets - predictions) ** 2)
    ss_tot = torch.sum((targets - torch.mean(targets)) ** 2)
    r2 = 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)
    
    print(f"Mean Squared Error (MSE): {mse.item():.6f}")
    print(f"Mean Absolute Error (MAE): {mae.item():.6f}")
    print(f"Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE): {rmse.item():.6f}")
    print(f"R-squared Score: {r2.item():.6f}")
    
    # MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error)
    mape = torch.mean(torch.abs((targets - predictions) / (targets + 1e-8))) * 100
    print(f"Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE): {mape.item():.2f}%")

class ModelEnsemble(nn.Module):
    """
    Ensemble of multiple models for improved prediction accuracy.
    Useful for critical energy applications requiring high reliability.
    """
    def __init__(self, models: List[nn.Module], weights: Optional[List[float]] = None):
        super(ModelEnsemble, self).__init__()
        self.models = nn.ModuleList(models)
        
        if weights is None:
            self.weights = [1.0 / len(models)] * len(models)
        else:
            self.weights = weights
            
    def forward(self, *args, **kwargs) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass through all models and combine predictions.
        """
        predictions = []
        for model in self.models:
            pred = model(*args, **kwargs)
            predictions.append(pred)
        
        # Weighted average
        ensemble_pred = sum(w * p for w, p in zip(self.weights, predictions))
        return ensemble_pred


def calculate_energy_metrics(predictions: torch.Tensor, 
                            targets: torch.Tensor,
                            peak_hours: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> dict:
    """
    Calculate comprehensive metrics for energy prediction tasks.
    
    Args:
        predictions: Model predictions
        targets: Ground truth values
        peak_hours: Binary mask for peak hours (optional)
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary of metrics
    """
    metrics = {}
    
    # Basic metrics
    mse = torch.mean((predictions - targets) ** 2)
    mae = torch.mean(torch.abs(predictions - targets))
    rmse = torch.sqrt(mse)
    
    metrics['mse'] = mse.item()
    metrics['mae'] = mae.item()
    metrics['rmse'] = rmse.item()
    
    # R-squared
    ss_res = torch.sum((targets - predictions) ** 2)
    ss_tot = torch.sum((targets - torch.mean(targets)) ** 2)
    r2 = 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)
    metrics['r2'] = r2.item()
    
    # MAPE
    mape = torch.mean(torch.abs((targets - predictions) / (targets + 1e-8))) * 100
    metrics['mape'] = mape.item()
    
    # Peak hour specific metrics
    if peak_hours is not None:
        peak_mask = peak_hours.bool()
        if peak_mask.sum() > 0:
            peak_mae = torch.mean(torch.abs(predictions[peak_mask] - targets[peak_mask]))
            metrics['peak_mae'] = peak_mae.item()
            
            off_peak_mask = ~peak_mask
            if off_peak_mask.sum() > 0:
                off_peak_mae = torch.mean(torch.abs(predictions[off_peak_mask] - targets[off_peak_mask]))
                metrics['off_peak_mae'] = off_peak_mae.item()
    
    return metrics


def save_checkpoint(model: nn.Module, optimizer: optim.Optimizer, 
                   epoch: int, loss: float, filepath: str):
    """
    Save model checkpoint with training state.
    """
    checkpoint = {
        'epoch': epoch,
        'model_state_dict': model.state_dict(),
        'optimizer_state_dict': optimizer.state_dict(),
        'loss': loss,
    }
    torch.save(checkpoint, filepath)
    print(f"Checkpoint saved to {filepath}")


def load_checkpoint(model: nn.Module, optimizer: optim.Optimizer, 
                   filepath: str) -> Tuple[nn.Module, optim.Optimizer, int, float]:
    """
    Load model checkpoint and restore training state.
    """
    checkpoint = torch.load(filepath)
    model.load_state_dict(checkpoint['model_state_dict'])
    optimizer.load_state_dict(checkpoint['optimizer_state_dict'])
    epoch = checkpoint['epoch']
    loss = checkpoint['loss']
    
    print(f"Checkpoint loaded from {filepath}")
    print(f"Resuming from epoch {epoch} with loss {loss:.6f}")
    
    return model, optimizer, epoch, loss


class EarlyStopping:
    """
    Early stopping to prevent overfitting.
    """
    def __init__(self, patience: int = 10, min_delta: float = 0.0001):
        self.patience = patience
        self.min_delta = min_delta
        self.counter = 0
        self.best_loss = None
        self.early_stop = False
        
    def __call__(self, val_loss: float):
        if self.best_loss is None:
            self.best_loss = val_loss
        elif val_loss > self.best_loss - self.min_delta:
            self.counter += 1
            if self.counter >= self.patience:
                self.early_stop = True
        else:
            self.best_loss = val_loss
            self.counter = 0


def predict_with_uncertainty(model: nn.Module, data: torch.Tensor, 
                            num_samples: int = 100, 
                            dropout_rate: float = 0.1) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Monte Carlo Dropout for uncertainty estimation.
    
    Args:
        model: Trained model
        data: Input data
        num_samples: Number of forward passes
        dropout_rate: Dropout rate for MC sampling
    
    Returns:
        Tuple of (mean_prediction, uncertainty)
    """
    model.train()  # Enable dropout
    
    predictions = []
    for _ in range(num_samples):
        with torch.no_grad():
            pred = model(data)
            predictions.append(pred)
    
    predictions = torch.stack(predictions)
    mean_pred = torch.mean(predictions, dim=0)
    uncertainty = torch.std(predictions, dim=0)
    
    return mean_pred, uncertainty

class EnergyDataNormalizer:
    """
    Normalizer for energy data with support for different scaling methods.
    """
    def __init__(self, method: str = 'standard'):
        """
        Args:
            method: 'standard', 'minmax', or 'robust'
        """
        self.method = method
        self.params = {}
        
    def fit(self, data: np.ndarray):
        """
        Fit normalizer to training data.
        """
        if self.method == 'standard':
            self.params['mean'] = np.mean(data, axis=0)
            self.params['std'] = np.std(data, axis=0) + 1e-8
        elif self.method == 'minmax':
            self.params['min'] = np.min(data, axis=0)
            self.params['max'] = np.max(data, axis=0)
            self.params['range'] = self.params['max'] - self.params['min'] + 1e-8
        elif self.method == 'robust':
            self.params['median'] = np.median(data, axis=0)
            self.params['q75'] = np.percentile(data, 75, axis=0)
            self.params['q25'] = np.percentile(data, 25, axis=0)
            self.params['iqr'] = self.params['q75'] - self.params['q25'] + 1e-8
            
    def transform(self, data: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Transform data using fitted parameters.
        """
        if self.method == 'standard':
            return (data - self.params['mean']) / self.params['std']
        elif self.method == 'minmax':
            return (data - self.params['min']) / self.params['range']
        elif self.method == 'robust':
            return (data - self.params['median']) / self.params['iqr']
            
    def inverse_transform(self, data: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Inverse transform to original scale.
        """
        if self.method == 'standard':
            return data * self.params['std'] + self.params['mean']
        elif self.method == 'minmax':
            return data * self.params['range'] + self.params['min']
        elif self.method == 'robust':
            return data * self.params['iqr'] + self.params['median']


def create_sequences(data: np.ndarray, seq_length: int, 
                     prediction_horizon: int = 1) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Create sequences for time series prediction.
    
    Args:
        data: Time series data (num_samples, num_features)
        seq_length: Length of input sequences
        prediction_horizon: Number of steps to predict ahead
    
    Returns:
        Tuple of (X, y) arrays
    """
    X, y = [], []
    
    for i in range(len(data) - seq_length - prediction_horizon + 1):
        X.append(data[i:i + seq_length])
        y.append(data[i + seq_length:i + seq_length + prediction_horizon])
    
    return np.array(X), np.array(y)


def add_temporal_features(timestamps: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Extract temporal features from timestamps.
    
    Args:
        timestamps: Array of datetime objects or Unix timestamps
    
    Returns:
        Array of temporal features
    """
    # Convert to datetime if needed
    if isinstance(timestamps[0], (int, float)):
        from datetime import datetime
        timestamps = [datetime.fromtimestamp(ts) for ts in timestamps]
    
    features = []
    for ts in timestamps:
        # Cyclical encoding for hour, day, month
        hour = ts.hour
        day = ts.day
        month = ts.month
        day_of_week = ts.weekday()
        
        # Sine/cosine encoding for cyclical features
        hour_sin = np.sin(2 * np.pi * hour / 24)
        hour_cos = np.cos(2 * np.pi * hour / 24)
        
        day_sin = np.sin(2 * np.pi * day / 31)
        day_cos = np.cos(2 * np.pi * day / 31)
        
        month_sin = np.sin(2 * np.pi * month / 12)
        month_cos = np.cos(2 * np.pi * month / 12)
        
        dow_sin = np.sin(2 * np.pi * day_of_week / 7)
        dow_cos = np.cos(2 * np.pi * day_of_week / 7)
        
        features.append([hour_sin, hour_cos, day_sin, day_cos, 
                        month_sin, month_cos, dow_sin, dow_cos])
    
    return np.array(features)

def plot_predictions(predictions: np.ndarray, targets: np.ndarray, 
                    title: str = "Predictions vs Actual"):
    """
    Plot predictions against actual values.
    Requires matplotlib (not imported to keep dependencies minimal).
    """
    try:
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        
        plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
        plt.plot(targets, label='Actual', alpha=0.7)
        plt.plot(predictions, label='Predicted', alpha=0.7)
        plt.xlabel('Time Steps')
        plt.ylabel('Value')
        plt.title(title)
        plt.legend()
        plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(f'{title.replace(" ", "_")}.png')
        print(f"Plot saved to {title.replace(' ', '_')}.png")
        plt.close()
    except ImportError:
        print("Matplotlib not available. Install with: pip install matplotlib")

class Config:
    """
    Configuration class for managing hyperparameters.
    """
    # Model hyperparameters
    HIDDEN_SIZE = 128
    NUM_LAYERS = 2
    DROPOUT = 0.2
    
    # Training hyperparameters
    BATCH_SIZE = 64
    LEARNING_RATE = 0.001
    NUM_EPOCHS = 100
    PATIENCE = 10
    
    # Data parameters
    SEQ_LENGTH = 24
    FORECAST_HORIZON = 24
    TRAIN_SPLIT = 0.8
    
    # Device
    DEVICE = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    
    @classmethod
    def to_dict(cls) -> dict:
        """Convert configuration to dictionary."""
        return {k: v for k, v in cls.__dict__.items() 
                if not k.startswith('_') and k.isupper()}
    
    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, config_dict: dict):
        """Load configuration from dictionary."""
        for key, value in config_dict.items():
            setattr(cls, key, value)

    energy_consumption = 100 + 20 * daily_pattern + 10 * weekly_pattern + trend + noise
    
    # Additional features (weather, temperature, etc.)
    features = np.random.randn(num_samples, num_features)
    features[:, 0] = energy_consumption  # Include consumption as a feature
    
    print(f"Generated {num_samples} samples with {num_features} features")
    
    # 2. Data preprocessing
    print("\n2. Preprocessing data...")
    normalizer = EnergyDataNormalizer(method='standard')
    normalizer.fit(features)
    normalized_features = normalizer.transform(features)
    
    # Create sequences
    seq_length = 24
    X, y = create_sequences(normalized_features, seq_length, prediction_horizon=1)
    
    print(f"Created sequences - X shape: {X.shape}, y shape: {y.shape}")
    
    # 3. Split data
    print("\n3. Splitting data into train/validation/test sets...")
    train_size = int(0.7 * len(X))
    val_size = int(0.15 * len(X))
    
    X_train, y_train = X[:train_size], y[:train_size]
    X_val, y_val = X[train_size:train_size + val_size], y[train_size:train_size + val_size]
    X_test, y_test = X[train_size + val_size:], y[train_size + val_size:]
    
    print(f"Train: {len(X_train)}, Val: {len(X_val)}, Test: {len(X_test)}")
    
    # 4. Create data loaders
    print("\n4. Creating data loaders...")
    train_dataset = TensorDataset(
        torch.FloatTensor(X_train),
        torch.FloatTensor(y_train[:, 0, 0])  # First step, first feature
    )
    val_dataset = TensorDataset(
        torch.FloatTensor(X_val),
        torch.FloatTensor(y_val[:, 0, 0])
    )
    test_dataset = TensorDataset(
        torch.FloatTensor(X_test),
        torch.FloatTensor(y_test[:, 0, 0])
    )
    
    train_loader = DataLoader(train_dataset, batch_size=64, shuffle=True)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_dataset, batch_size=64)
    test_loader = DataLoader(test_dataset, batch_size=64)
    
    # 5. Initialize model
    print("\n5. Initializing model...")
    model = EnergyConsumptionPredictor(
        input_size=num_features,
        hidden_size=128,
        num_layers=2,
        output_size=1
    )
    
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    model = model.to(device)
    print(f"Model initialized on {device}")
    print(f"Total parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()):,}")
    
    # 6. Training
    print("\n6. Training model...")
    optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn.MSELoss()
    early_stopping = EarlyStopping(patience=10)
    
    train_losses = []
    val_losses = []
    
    num_epochs = 20
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        # Training
        model.train()
        train_loss = 0.0
        for batch_x, batch_y in train_loader:
            batch_x, batch_y = batch_x.to(device), batch_y.to(device)
            
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = model(batch_x).squeeze()
            loss = criterion(output, batch_y)
            loss.backward()
            
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)
            optimizer.step()
            
            train_loss += loss.item()
        
        train_loss /= len(train_loader)
        train_losses.append(train_loss)
        
        # Validation
        model.eval()
        val_loss = 0.0
        with torch.no_grad():
            for batch_x, batch_y in val_loader:
                batch_x, batch_y = batch_x.to(device), batch_y.to(device)
                output = model(batch_x).squeeze()
                loss = criterion(output, batch_y)
                val_loss += loss.item()
        
        val_loss /= len(val_loader)
        val_losses.append(val_loss)
        
        print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs} - Train Loss: {train_loss:.6f}, Val Loss: {val_loss:.6f}")
        
        # Early stopping
        early_stopping(val_loss)
        if early_stopping.early_stop:
            print("Early stopping triggered")
            break
    
    # 7. Evaluation
    print("\n7. Evaluating model on test set...")
    model.eval()
    all_predictions = []
    all_targets = []
    
    with torch.no_grad():
        for batch_x, batch_y in test_loader:
            batch_x = batch_x.to(device)
            output = model(batch_x).squeeze()
            all_predictions.append(output.cpu())
            all_targets.append(batch_y)
    
    predictions = torch.cat(all_predictions).numpy()
    targets = torch.cat(all_targets).numpy()
    
    # Calculate metrics
    metrics = calculate_energy_metrics(
        torch.FloatTensor(predictions),
        torch.FloatTensor(targets)
    )
    
    print("\nTest Set Metrics:")
    for metric_name, metric_value in metrics.items():
        print(f"  {metric_name.upper()}: {metric_value:.6f}")
    
    # 8. Uncertainty estimation
    print("\n8. Estimating prediction uncertainty...")
    sample_batch = next(iter(test_loader))[0][:10].to(device)
    mean_pred, uncertainty = predict_with_uncertainty(model, sample_batch, num_samples=50)
    
    print(f"Sample predictions with uncertainty:")
    for i in range(5):
        print(f"  Prediction {i+1}: {mean_pred[i].item():.4f} ± {uncertainty[i].item():.4f}")
    
    # 9. Save model
    print("\n9. Saving model...")
    save_checkpoint(model, optimizer, num_epochs, val_losses[-1], 'energy_model_checkpoint.pth')
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("Pipeline completed successfully!")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    return model, metrics, train_losses, val_losses

class EnergyPredictionService:
    """
    Production-ready service for energy prediction.
    Handles model loading, preprocessing, and prediction.
    """
    def __init__(self, model_path: str, normalizer_params: dict):
        """
        Args:
            model_path: Path to saved model checkpoint
            normalizer_params: Dictionary with normalization parameters
        """
        self.device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
        
        # Load model
        self.model = EnergyConsumptionPredictor(
            input_size=10, hidden_size=128, num_layers=2, output_size=1
        )
        checkpoint = torch.load(model_path, map_location=self.device)
        self.model.load_state_dict(checkpoint['model_state_dict'])
        self.model.to(self.device)
        self.model.eval()
        
        # Setup normalizer
        self.normalizer = EnergyDataNormalizer(method='standard')
        self.normalizer.params = normalizer_params
        
        print(f"Model loaded successfully on {self.device}")
    
    def predict(self, input_data: np.ndarray, 
                return_uncertainty: bool = False) -> dict:
        """
        Make prediction on new data.
        
        Args:
            input_data: Input features (seq_len, num_features)
            return_uncertainty: Whether to return uncertainty estimates
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with predictions and optional uncertainty
        """
        # Preprocess
        normalized_data = self.normalizer.transform(input_data)
        input_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(normalized_data).unsqueeze(0).to(self.device)
        
        # Predict
        with torch.no_grad():
            if return_uncertainty:
                mean_pred, uncertainty = predict_with_uncertainty(
                    self.model, input_tensor, num_samples=50
                )
                prediction = mean_pred.cpu().numpy()[0, 0]
                uncertainty_val = uncertainty.cpu().numpy()[0, 0]
            else:
                prediction = self.model(input_tensor).cpu().numpy()[0, 0]
                uncertainty_val = None
        
        # Denormalize (if needed)
        # prediction = self.normalizer.inverse_transform(prediction)
        
        result = {
            'prediction': float(prediction),
            'timestamp': np.datetime64('now').astype(str)
        }
        
        if return_uncertainty:
            result['uncertainty'] = float(uncertainty_val)
        
        return result
    
    def batch_predict(self, input_batch: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Make predictions on a batch of inputs.
        
        Args:
            input_batch: Batch of inputs (batch_size, seq_len, num_features)
        
        Returns:
            Array of predictions
        """
        normalized_batch = np.array([
            self.normalizer.transform(sample) for sample in input_batch
        ])
        
        input_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(normalized_batch).to(self.device)
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            predictions = self.model(input_tensor).cpu().numpy()
        
        return predictions

def benchmark_inference_speed(model: nn.Module, input_shape: Tuple[int, ...], 
                              num_iterations: int = 100):
    """
    Benchmark model inference speed.
    
    Args:
        model: Model to benchmark
        input_shape: Shape of input tensor
        num_iterations: Number of iterations for benchmarking
    """
    import time
    
    device = next(model.parameters()).device
    model.eval()
    
    # Warmup
    dummy_input = torch.randn(*input_shape).to(device)
    for _ in range(10):
        with torch.no_grad():
            _ = model(dummy_input)
    
    # Benchmark
    start_time = time.time()
    for _ in range(num_iterations):
        with torch.no_grad():
            _ = model(dummy_input)
    
    if device.type == 'cuda':
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
    
    end_time = time.time()
    
    avg_time = (end_time - start_time) / num_iterations
    throughput = 1.0 / avg_time
    
    print(f"\nInference Benchmark Results:")
    print(f"  Average inference time: {avg_time*1000:.2f} ms")
    print(f"  Throughput: {throughput:.2f} samples/second")
    print(f"  Device: {device}")

class AttentionVisualizer:
    """
    Visualize attention weights for interpretability.
    """
    @staticmethod
    def extract_attention_weights(model: nn.Module, 
                                  input_data: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Extract attention weights from model.
        Note: This assumes the model has an attention mechanism.
        """
        # This is model-specific
        # For models with attention layers, hook into the attention computation
        attention_weights = None
        
        def hook_fn(module, input, output):
            nonlocal attention_weights
            attention_weights = output
        
        # Register hook (example for models with named attention layer)
        if hasattr(model, 'attention'):
            handle = model.attention.register_forward_hook(hook_fn)
            
            with torch.no_grad():
                _ = model(input_data)
            
            handle.remove()
        
        return attention_weights
    
    @staticmethod
    def plot_attention_heatmap(attention_weights: np.ndarray, 
                              save_path: str = 'attention_heatmap.png'):
        """
        Plot attention weights as a heatmap.
        """
        try:
            import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
            import seaborn as sns
            
            plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
            sns.heatmap(attention_weights, cmap='viridis', cbar=True)
            plt.title('Attention Weights Heatmap')
            plt.xlabel('Time Steps')
            plt.ylabel('Samples')
            plt.tight_layout()
            plt.savefig(save_path)
            print(f"Attention heatmap saved to {save_path}")
            plt.close()
        except ImportError:
            print("Matplotlib/Seaborn not available for visualization")

# ============================================================================
# Additional Example: Multi-Task Learning
# ============================================================================

class MultiTaskEnergyModel(nn.Module):
    """
    Multi-task model for simultaneous prediction of multiple energy metrics.
    Shares representations across tasks for improved efficiency.
    """
    def __init__(self, input_size: int, hidden_size: int = 128):
        super(MultiTaskEnergyModel, self).__init__()
        
        # Shared encoder
        self.shared_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_size),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Task-specific heads
        self.consumption_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_size, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 1)
        )
        
        self.cost_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_size, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 1),
            nn.ReLU()  # Cost is positive
        )
        
        self.carbon_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_size, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 1),
            nn.ReLU()  # Carbon is positive
        )
        
        self.peak_classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_size, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()  # Binary: peak or off-peak
        )
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
        """
        Args:
            x: Input features (batch_size, input_size)
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with predictions for each task
        """
        shared_features = self.shared_encoder(x)
        
        return {
            'consumption': self.consumption_head(shared_features),
            'cost': self.cost_head(shared_features),
            'carbon': self.carbon_head(shared_features),
            'is_peak': self.peak_classifier(shared_features)
        }


class MultiTaskLoss(nn.Module):
    """
    Combined loss for multi-task learning with learnable task weights.
    """
    def __init__(self, num_tasks: int):
        super(MultiTaskLoss, self).__init__()
        # Learnable task weights (using uncertainty weighting)
        self.log_vars = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(num_tasks))
        
    def forward(self, predictions: dict, targets: dict) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, dict]:
        """
        Args:
            predictions: Dictionary of predictions for each task
            targets: Dictionary of ground truth for each task
        
        Returns:
            Tuple of (total_loss, individual_losses)
        """
        mse = nn.MSELoss()
        bce = nn.BCELoss()
        
        # Individual losses
        consumption_loss = mse(predictions['consumption'], targets['consumption'])
        cost_loss = mse(predictions['cost'], targets['cost'])
        carbon_loss = mse(predictions['carbon'], targets['carbon'])
        peak_loss = bce(predictions['is_peak'], targets['is_peak'])
        
        # Weighted combination (uncertainty weighting)
        precision_consumption = torch.exp(-self.log_vars[0])
        precision_cost = torch.exp(-self.log_vars[1])
        precision_carbon = torch.exp(-self.log_vars[2])
        precision_peak = torch.exp(-self.log_vars[3])
        
        total_loss = (precision_consumption * consumption_loss + self.log_vars[0] +
                     precision_cost * cost_loss + self.log_vars[1] +
                     precision_carbon * carbon_loss + self.log_vars[2] +
                     precision_peak * peak_loss + self.log_vars[3])
        
        individual_losses = {
            'consumption': consumption_loss.item(),
            'cost': cost_loss.item(),
            'carbon': carbon_loss.item(),
            'peak': peak_loss.item()
        }
        
        return total_loss, individual_losses

def transfer_learning_example():
    """
    Demonstrates transfer learning for adapting a model trained on one
    region to another region with limited data.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("TRANSFER LEARNING EXAMPLE")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Pretrained model (source domain)
    print("\n1. Loading pretrained model from source region...")
    source_model = EnergyConsumptionPredictor(
        input_size=10, hidden_size=128, num_layers=2, output_size=1
    )
    
    # Simulate pretrained weights
    print("   Model initialized with pretrained weights")
    
    # Target domain model
    print("\n2. Creating model for target region...")
    target_model = EnergyConsumptionPredictor(
        input_size=10, hidden_size=128, num_layers=2, output_size=1
    )
    
    # Copy pretrained weights
    target_model.load_state_dict(source_model.state_dict())
    
    # Freeze early layers
    print("\n3. Freezing early layers...")
    for name, param in target_model.named_parameters():
        if 'lstm' in name:
            param.requires_grad = False
    
    print("   LSTM layers frozen, only fine-tuning attention and FC layers")
    
    # Fine-tune on target domain
    print("\n4. Fine-tuning on target region data...")
    trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in target_model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
    total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in target_model.parameters())
    print(f"   Trainable parameters: {trainable_params:,} / {total_params:,}")
    
    # Use lower learning rate for fine-tuning
    optimizer = optim.Adam(
        filter(lambda p: p.requires_grad, target_model.parameters()),
        lr=0.0001
    )
    
    print("\n   Fine-tuning complete!")
    print("=" * 80)
